look_here_first: Find TERMINAL whorls of LONG narrow trumpet-shaped flowers, usually ~38–48 mm. The top pair of opposite leaves/bracts often FUSES into a round disk below the head. But this is also possible in white/Texas honeysuckle—measure the narrow elongated trumpet versus L. albiflora's short two-lipped flower.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Woody perennial twining or trailing vine with opposite simple oval to elliptic leaves; terminal upper pair often connate and perfoliate, bluish/glaucous underside possible.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Opposite simple leaves with entire to near-entire margins; petiole lengths and fused terminal bracts vary by species.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Showy cluster of long narrow tubular 5-lobed corollas in terminal whorls, often red/orange outside and yellow inside; tube is far longer relative to small lobes.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Red-orange to scarlet berries; not unique among native comparison.
